welcome.title: FreeC Tier setup
welcome.intro: Computers talk to each other through Steam, so the client connects under a game's ID. Two steps — and you never have to come back to this.
welcome.step1_title: Add the app to your Steam library
welcome.step1_text: FreeC Tier connects under AppID {app_id}{game}. The license is free, but Steam only grants it on request. Without it the Steam client refuses the connection, and nothing else shows why.
welcome.add_note: Steam grants the license and offers a download — you can cancel it, the app stays in your library.
welcome.in_library: The app is already in your library — step done.

mtu.title: Virtual adapter MTU
mtu.custom_hint: Custom value: {value} bytes. Change it only if a game does not work with the presets.
mtu.hint_1280: Recommended: the size games expect on a local network.
mtu.hint_1152: A whole packet fits one Steam datagram — fewer losses on a poor connection, but some games expect a larger size.
mtu.hint_1500: Like a regular Ethernet network. Steam splits large packets into parts.
mtu.applies: Applies immediately, including networks already running. Restarting the game is best.

webview2.caption: FreeC Tier — WebView2 setup
webview2.question:
The FreeC Tier interface needs the Microsoft WebView2 Runtime component — regular Windows 10/11 already has it, but it was not found on this system.

Install it now? An internet connection is needed (about 2 MB).
webview2.failed:
Could not install the WebView2 Runtime.

Install it manually from Microsoft's official page and start FreeC Tier again. The download page will open now.
event.auto_on_conflict: The network did not turn on automatically: subnet conflict
event.auto_on_failed: The network did not turn on automatically: {error}
error.steam_signed_out: Steam is not signed in — sign in to your account
error.steam_required: Start Steam and sign in to do this
error.owner_pending: Waiting for the owner's answer; try again in a few seconds
peer_end.no_steam: no connection to the Steam network
steam_wait.not_running: Steam is not running — start the client and sign in.
steam_wait.starting: Steam is still starting — wait for the client to open.
steam_wait.signed_out: Steam is running, but sign-in has not finished — sign in and turn off “Offline” mode.
steam_hint.other_account: Steam is running under another Windows account — restart the computer to clear the stuck process.
steam_hint.several_processes: Several Steam processes are running and one of them is stuck — restart the computer to clear it.
steam_hint.not_in_library: It looks like app {app_id}, which FreeC Tier works through, is not in your Steam library. Open store.steampowered.com/app/{app_id} and press “Play” — it is free and there is nothing to download. If it is already in your library, the cause is external: usually an antivirus, so add FreeC Tier and Steam to its exclusions.
steam_hint.restart_unelevated: Restart Steam: sign out and sign in again. If that does not help, restart FreeC Tier without administrator rights.
steam_hint.restart_uac: Restart Steam: sign out and sign in again. If that does not help, turn on User Account Control (UAC) and restart both apps.
steam_hint.antivirus: Steam appears to run correctly, but the connection to it is blocked. This is usually an antivirus — add FreeC Tier and Steam to its exclusions. If that does not help, restart the computer.
